title: Overseas "visa processing" fee to a personal account vs. registered agent explaining the official emigration route
summary: A caller from SafarWays Overseas Manpower phones about a facilities-technician job with Dunecrest Facilities Management in a Gulf country. In the fraud case, the caller asks for a large "visa processing" payment to an individual's account before any employer interview, saying the worker will travel on a visit visa and "convert" it later. In the legitimate case, the caller is a registered recruiting agent who gives a licence number, explains the employer interview, contract, work visa, and emigration clearance, and states a capped service charge payable only after selection, to the agency's account against a receipt.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a tradesperson (ITI diploma or equivalent experience) who uploaded a CV on NaukriHub or dropped it at a walk-in; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: HVAC / facilities technician, two-year contract, monthly salary [AMOUNT_1] (₹45,000–₹75,000 equivalent), accommodation mentioned.
Both callers mention the CV, the country, the role, and the salary. Both mention money; the pair differs in when, to whom, and on what terms.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller demands a large payment to an individual's account before any employer selection, for travel on a visit visa rather than a work visa, bypassing the official emigration process.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect the "visa processing" money; there is no job or work visa.
stable_facts: Payment: [AMOUNT_2] (₹80,000–₹2,00,000), called "visa processing and ticket charges", half now.
Paid to an account in an individual's name, [ACCT_LAST4], or [UPI_ID_1].
Caller says the worker will fly on a visit visa and the company will "convert it to a work visa" after arrival.
No licence number, no employer interview, no written contract before payment.

legitimate.label_rationale: A registered recruiting agent explains the official route (employer interview, signed contract, work visa, emigration clearance) and a capped, receipted service charge payable only after selection to the agency.

stable_facts: SafarWays gives its recruiting-agent licence number [LICENCE_ID] (proposed new placeholder; see note under Evidence references) and suggests the recipient check it on the government emigration portal.
Dunecrest holds a trade test and interview in [CITY] on a stated date.
After selection: signed employment contract, work visa, emigration clearance, pre-departure orientation.

SafarWays charges a service charge [AMOUNT_3] (₹10,000–₹20,000, below both conflicting cap figures in C14; stated only as "within the government cap") only after selection and visa, to the agency's registered bank account, with a receipt. The employer bears airfare and accommodation.

markers.text: Licence number stated and recipient invited to verify it
Employer interview/trade test before any offer
Work visa and signed contract; no visit-visa shortcut
Service charge disclosed, capped, after selection, to the agency account with receipt

cooperative.fraud: Agrees to transfer and asks for the account details again
cooperative.legitimate: Confirms attendance at the trade test and asks which documents to bring

clarifying.fraud: Asks why a visit visa and whether the money is refundable
clarifying.legitimate: Asks what the trade test involves and when the service charge is due

resistant.fraud: Says they will pay only after seeing a contract
resistant.legitimate: Says they cannot afford the service charge and asks if it can be reduced

suspicious.fraud: Says they heard visit-visa job offers are illegal and asks for a licence number
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how to confirm the licence number is genuine

fraud: caller gives a vague or made-up licence claim and recipient ends the call
legitimate: recipient says they will verify the licence first and the caller encourages it
caller repeats that no money is due before selection.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may reduce the first instalment, claim seats are filling, or promise a refund. They must not switch to asking for OTPs, passwords, or remote access. The legitimate caller must not ask for any payment before selection, must not ask for money to a personal account, and must not change the service charge terms after the branch.

must_preserve: role, country, contract length, and salary identical across _F and _L
_F upfront payment to an individual's account at turn 7 with visit-visa framing
_L licence number, trade test, work visa, and post-selection receipted service charge
may_vary: destination country (Gulf region, unnamed or generic)
must_not_emit: working account numbers or UPI IDs

ambiguities: A payment request is not by itself evidence: _L contains a disclosed service charge. The label rests on timing (before vs. after selection), recipient (individual vs. agency), visa type, and receipt.
The amount is not evidence; _F and _L ranges overlap at the low end on purpose if _F quotes only the first instalment.
Do not state a specific cap figure; sources conflict (C14).
An agency name alone does not confirm registration; the caller's stated licence number is a marker, not proof.

evidence_references.claim: Overseas recruitment must go through MEA-registered agents verifiable on eMigrate (C13)
Recruiting-agent service charges are capped (C14; cite as "capped" only)
Valid offers come with a contract signed by employer, agent, and worker, on a work visa, not a tourist visa (CJ13)
Registered agents display a licence number and must issue receipts for service charges (CJ14)
Reputed foreign employers normally bear airfare, lodging, and insurance (CJ15)
Upfront payment is a red flag in fake job schemes (C11)
